episodes.180223: The first part of the day on June 30, 2023, was characterized by dangerous hot and humid conditions across most of Middle Tennessee as heat index values soared to 115 to 125 degrees. With these hot temperatures, an abundant amount of instability was in place across the area. With a mesoscale convective system (MCS) developing over Illinois and Indiana and diving southward, it moved into an environment that was favorable for severe thunderstorms. Damaging winds were the main hazards with this line of thunderstorms with several wind damage reports received through the evening hours.
episodes.180225: A few strong to severe storms occurred over portions of eastern NM. These produced two reports of hail at Maxwell and Yates during the afternoon of June 30th.
episodes.180233: Showers and thunderstorms developed around a surface trough on the afternoon and evening. Slow moving thunderstorms led to some instances of flash flooding across central Virginia.
episodes.180234: Showers and thunderstorms developed around a surface trough on the afternoon and evening. A slow moving thunderstorms led to an isolated instance of flash flooding in Prince Georges County Maryland.
episodes.180235: A line of thunderstorms tracked eastward across Middle Tennessee early in the afternoon of July 1, 2023. With an abundant amount of instability in place, these thunderstorms quickly became severe with damaging winds the primary threat. Wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph were common as they marched eastward and numerous reports were received of downed trees and powerlines. Fortunately, no injuries were reported. Otherwise, excessive heat across portions of the area continued as a few locations reported heat index values exceeding 110 degrees until the thunderstorms arrived.
episodes.180245: Multiple clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms erupted during the midday hours lasting through the afternoon across much of north Alabama. The thunderstorms produced wind damage at multiple locations.
episodes.180246: Multiple clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms erupted during the midday hours which moved east across southern middle Tennessee. The thunderstorms produced wind damage in Lincoln, Moore and Franklin Counties.
episodes.180272: A storm system approached the region from the southern Rockies and Desert Southwest. In addition, rich Gulf of Mexico moisture spread northward into the South Plains. As lift from the disturbance reached the moisture, scattered thunderstorms developed across the southwest Texas Panhandle and western South Plains on the afternoon of the 30th. The thunderstorms grew upscale into clusters and eventually a line of storms as they propagated eastward through the late afternoon and evening hours. Torrential rainfall accompanied the most intense activity, which led to flooded roadways in areas. One band of concentrated heavy rain became anchored from north-central Hockley County to southeast Lamb County, north of Levelland (Hockley County) to southeast of Littlefield (Lamb County). Several inches of fell in over the course of a couple hours, making travel difficult to impossible for a time along US Highways 84 and 385. Additional heavy rain was more transient in nature, but still created at least minor flooding in spots, including parts of Lubbock (Lubbock County). As the thunderstorm coverage and its associated rain cooled outflows grew in size, wind gusts increased. A couple of locations in the Rolling Plains recorded severe wind gusts.
episodes.180328: During the early overnight hours of June 30th a series of storms moved through central Indiana causing sporadic wind damage.  The most notable damage of the event occurred across Decatur county with widespread tree damage and an isolated area with over 250 downed trees. This event continued into July 1st.
episodes.180329: This episode is a continuation of the episode from June 30th with two rounds of storms.  The first round occurred during the overnight hours of the 30th into the 1st with a few reports of damaging wind gusts.  The most impressive area of wind damage was across Decatur county.  Storms reinitiated across western Indiana during the evening hours of the 1st with flash flooding and additional wind damage.
episodes.180420: Between 7-10 p.m. CDT on this Friday evening, a compact mesoscale convective system (MCS) with an initially intense, embedded supercell rolled from west-to-east across primarily Rooks, Osborne and Mitchell counties in this North Central Kansas area, producing several reports of damaging winds/large hail (including up to tennis ball size). This severe storm cluster first organized in northeast Colorado during the early-mid afternoon before traversing northwest Kansas mid-late afternoon and eventually infiltrating mainly the northern half of Rooks County between 7-8 p.m. CDT, during which time the dominant supercell reached its peak intensity within the local area. In Rooks County, there were several reports of hail ranging from ping pong ball up to tennis ball size, and broken windows were reported at a business south of Stockton along Highway 183. Also in Rooks County, damaging winds estimated up to 70 MPH caused tree damage in Damar and overturned a camper at Webster State Park. Between 8-9 p.m. CDT, the dominant supercell weakened slightly over Osborne County as it merged with other convection drifting north out of central Kansas, but it still yielded a report of ping pong ball size hail eight miles south-southeast of Osborne. Finally, between 9-10 p.m. CDT the most intense convection transitioned to a more linear mode as it crossed Mitchell County, yielding an unofficial mesonet-measured wind gust of 59 MPH seven miles east of Tipton. Although the main storm cluster departed east of the local area by 10 p.m. CDT, trailing showers/weaker storms lingered for at least a few hours before convection departed North Central Kansas for the night. Rainfall-wise, although limited parts of the area received at least 1-2 inches in a short time, there were no reports of significant flooding. ||Turning to the meteorological background, this was a fairly classic setup for early-summer MCS development. In the mid-upper levels, the primary driver was a shortwave trough slowly migrating from the CO/WY/NE border area into the Central Plains over the course of the afternoon-evening. At the surface, North Central Kansas resided slightly north of a generally west-east oriented quasi-stationary front stretched from southern into east central Kansas. Locally, the early evening pre-convective environment was defined by temperatures in the 80s and dewpoints in the 60s (F), with mesoscale parameters featuring moderate mixed-layer CAPE of 1000-2000 J/kg but fairly strong deep-layer wind shear of 40-45 knots.
episodes.180467: A lone thunderstorm collapsed in Elkhart County and downed trees in Middlebury.
episodes.180517: A severe thunderstorm impacted the Laurel Highlands and localized flooding impacted the city of Altoona during the afternoon of July 1, 2023. Scattered thunderstorm developed in a modest CAPE environment (1000-1500 J/kg) and modest shear environment ahead of an approaching mid-level trough.
episodes.180607: Isolated severe thunderstorm cells formed explosively during the late afternoon hours. The storms rapidly intensified into destructive hailstorms, producing golf ball to baseball size hail for sustained periods of time. During the evening, damaging winds became the main hazard as a bowing line of storms moved east-southeast across the Mount Vernon area. The storms formed in an extremely unstable air mass south of an outflow boundary that was generated from earlier storms well to the north. Strong daytime heating and high dew points in the mid 70's yielded mixed-layer capes around 5000 j/kg. Wind shear was adequate for organized storm structures. Effective shear values averaged around 30 knots.
episodes.180611: Thunderstorm cells rapidly developed over northwest Kentucky. Large hail was the main hazard with the initial thunderstorm cells in the late afternoon hours. The cells organized into a complex of storms that moved quickly south-southeast across the Pennyrile region of west Kentucky. Strong to locally damaging winds accompanied the complex of storms. The storms formed in an extremely unstable air mass south of an outflow boundary that was generated from earlier storms well to the north. Strong daytime heating and high dew points in the mid to upper 70's yielded mixed-layer capes around 5500 j/kg. Deep-layer wind shear was very marginal for organized storm structures. Effective shear values averaged 20 to 30 knots.
episodes.180620: An upper level disturbance moving through the Ohio Valley produced scattered showers and thunderstorms during the early morning hours.
episodes.180621: An upper level disturbance moving through the Ohio Valley produced scattered showers and thunderstorms during the early morning hours.
episodes.180623: An upper level disturbance moving through the Ohio Valley produced scattered showers and thunderstorms during the early morning hours.
episodes.180642: An outbreak of severe thunderstorms occurred during the late afternoon and early evening. There were scattered to numerous reports of wind damage, including a couple of destructive wind events with speeds to 80 mph or greater. The storms initially formed as cells or small clusters, which produced large hail and marginally severe wind. Later in the outbreak, the storms evolved into a couple of bowing lines with rather widespread damaging winds. The storms developed in response to a rather amplified 500 mb shortwave trough that progressed east into Iowa and Missouri by nightfall. With daytime heating, the atmosphere became very unstable in the afternoon. Mixed-layer capes were around 3000 j/kg late in the day. A belt of 35 to 45 knot mid-level west-southwesterly winds resulted in sufficient deep-layer wind shear for organized storm structures.
episodes.180643: A couple of short lines of thunderstorms moved southeast across southwest Indiana during the overnight hours into the early and mid-morning hours. These two lines of storms were associated with strong gusty winds and a few tree damage reports. The storms occurred under a belt of moderately strong southwest mid-level winds, well ahead of an amplifying 500 mb trough over the western high Plains. A southwest surface wind provided an ample supply of moist and unstable air.
episodes.180645: A couple of lines of thunderstorms moved northeast across far western Kentucky during the late afternoon and evening hours. The first line consisted of semi-discrete cells, one of which was associated with a weak tornado that tracked across the Kentucky Lake area. The second line was associated with a few isolated marginally severe wind gusts to 60 mph. The storms developed in response to a rather amplified 500 mb shortwave trough that progressed east into Iowa and Missouri by nightfall. With daytime heating, the atmosphere became very unstable in the afternoon. Mixed-layer capes were around 3000 j/kg late in the day. A belt of 35 to 45 knot mid-level west-southwesterly winds resulted in sufficient deep-layer wind shear for organized storm structures. An embedded tornado occurred in the vicinity of a residual outflow boundary arcing west from storms over central Kentucky.
episodes.180646: A bowing line of severe thunderstorms moved rapidly east-northeast out of southeast Illinois across extreme southwest Indiana. This line produced wind gusts up to 70 mph from the Wabash River east to the Evansville metro area. The storms developed in response to a rather amplified 500 mb shortwave trough that progressed east into Iowa and Missouri by nightfall. With daytime heating, the atmosphere became very unstable in the afternoon. Mixed-layer capes were around 3000 j/kg late in the day. A belt of 35 to 45 knot mid-level west-southwesterly winds resulted in sufficient deep-layer wind shear for organized storm structures.
episodes.180647: A line of thunderstorms moved eastward across parts of southeast Missouri during the late afternoon hours. Isolated damaging wind gusts occurred with this line, which stayed mainly to the north of U.S. Highway 60. Shortly thereafter, a cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms formed south of Highway 60. These storms produced isolated wind damage shortly before crossing the Mississippi River into Kentucky. The storms developed in response to a rather amplified 500 mb shortwave trough that progressed east into Iowa and Missouri by nightfall. With daytime heating, the atmosphere became very unstable in the afternoon. Mixed-layer capes were around 3000 j/kg late in the day. A belt of 35 to 45 knot mid-level west-southwesterly winds resulted in sufficient deep-layer wind shear for organized storm structures.
episodes.180825: A weak surface trough was present across portions of the Piedmont of central North Carolina in an otherwise high pressure regime. Isolated to scattered showers and storms developed in the late afternoon to early evening over the western Piedmont, tracking east and south over the central Piedmont and Sandhills during the late evening and overnight hours. A few of the storms became severe in Chatham and Orange Counties, along with flash flooding over Durham.
episodes.181280: A slow-moving frontal boundary interacting with a seasonably warm and moist airmass triggered a cluster of thunderstorms along the I-70 corridor during the late evening of June 30th.  The storms produced hail as large as quarters in Mattoon in Coles County.
episodes.181334: A loosely organized area of thunderstorms developed along propagating outflow from the Texas Panhandle into portions of western and southwestern Oklahoma. A few severe wind gusts were noted beneath the strongest developing thunderstorm cores.
episodes.181505: Early morning thunderstorm complex clips southwest Virginia bringing strong to severe thunderstorm wind gusts.
episodes.181506: A mesoscale convective system brings scattered damaging winds to the southern Tennessee Valley in East Tennessee.
episodes.181568: Summer thunderstorms developed across primarily south central and southwestern Montana in early July. Several of these storms produced large hail and strong gusty winds. The strongest storms impacted the Bozeman area and Canyon Ferry Lake recreational area.
episodes.181597: A weak wave aloft interacting with light winds and abundant moisture resulted in slow moving thunderstorms across the Finger Lakes late on the afternoon of the 1st. As storms merged together, they moved even slower with multiple rounds of heavy rain impacting portions of Ontario county. There were multiple reports of flooded roads in the Canandaigua and Geneva areas.
episodes.181605: An area of showers and thunderstorms developed over southwestern Virginia and intensified as they moved southeast into North Carolina. The line of showers and thunderstorms tracked east-southeast across the central North Carolina Piedmont and into the Sandhills, producing numerous damaging wind reports.
episodes.181679: Strong to severe storms developed during the afternoon and evening over central and south central Missouri, within the warm sector of a low pressure system that tracked across central Missouri. Hail up to the size of golf balls and sporadic wind damage to trees and powerlines occurred over Dent, Howell, Miller, Texas, and Wright Counties. A low water crossing flooded near Bakersfield in Ozark County.
episodes.181769: A north south oriented mesoscale convective system moving from west to east brings severe thunderstorm winds to western North Carolina.
episodes.181793: Scattered severe thunderstorms caused wind damage with gusts estimated as high as 90 mph during the afternoon and evening hours of June 30th.
episodes.181856: A pressure trough ignited a few thunderstorms that produced spotty wind damage during the late afternoon hours.
episodes.181859: A pressure trough ignited a few thunderstorms that produced spotty wind damage during the late afternoon hours.
episodes.181860: A pressure trough ignited a few thunderstorms that produced spotty wind damage during the late afternoon hours.
episodes.181880: In the early afternoon of the 30th, storms from Colorado crossed into Kansas along I-70. These storms caused widespread wind damage and up to 2 inch in diameter hail. The highest measured wind gust was 79.4 mph at Hill City and then the station promptly stopped reporting winds. One injury did occur when a vehicle was blown off of the road. Torrential rainfall also lead to localized flash flooding.
episodes.181924: Long duration rainfall over western Douglas County led to minor street flooding in Valley and Waterloo.
episodes.181933: A pressure trough ignited a few thunderstorms that produced gale-force winds over portions of the tidal Potomac River.
episodes.182040: A potent shortwave trough was ejecting into the southern Great Plains by evening. This resulted in the development of a broken line of strong to severe thunderstorms from the Stockton Plateau to the Permian Basin. Several severe wind reports, localized wind damage, and flash flooding were reported with a few of these thunderstorms.
episodes.182105: A warm front lifted north into southeastern Illinois during the afternoon, resulting in widespread thunderstorm development along the front. One severe wind gust was measured in Lawrence County, but no wind damage was reported.
episodes.182477: Earlier in the day on June 30th, an MCS made its way across southern Iowa and northern Missouri into north-central Illinois. As it moved eastward, an outflow boundary moved south and interacted with a surface boundary stretching across central Missouri. There was a strong gradient of surface-based CAPE. Storms developed and followed that gradient and frontal boundary southeast across central Missouri into south central Illinois. The severe storms produced large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.182478: Earlier in the day on June 30th, an MCS made its way across southern Iowa and northern Missouri into north-central Illinois. As it moved eastward, an outflow boundary moved south and interacted with a surface boundary stretching across central Missouri. There was a strong gradient of surface-based CAPE. Storms developed and followed that gradient and frontal boundary southeast across central Missouri into south central Illinois. The severe storms produced large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.182586: Isolated severe thunderstorms produced wind gusts greater than 60 mph across portions of the Big Country.
episodes.182738: A few isolated thunderstorms produced some strong wind gusts.
episodes.182820: Thunderstorms that developed in western Kansas moved east into north central Kansas during the evening hours of June 30th. These storms produced wind gusts of 60 mph.|There was one report of wind damage when part of a roof was torn off of an outbuilding in near Kanopolis in Ellsworth County.
episodes.182845: On the morning of June 30th, a line of storms moved through far northern Missouri, producing 60 to 70 mph wind gusts. Then in the afternoon and evening of June 30th, storms brought large hail and damaging winds to much of Missouri, including softball sized hail in Lexington, MO.
episodes.182854: A line of storms brought 60 to 70 mph winds to portions of eastern KS (Leavenworth and Atchison Counties) on the evening of June 30th.
episodes.182892: A shortwave trough aided in the development of numerous afternoon strong to severe thunderstorms. These thunderstorms formed along the higher elevations and a remnant outflow boundary. Isolated large hail and severe wind gusts were reported.
episodes.183058: A small line of thunderstorms moved through the south central Texas Panhandle on the morning of the 1st. As these showers and thunderstorms started to die off after midnight, a severe wind gust occurred at the mesonet site located 15 NNW of Amarillo. This wind gust was likely the by product of a heat burst, not so much a strong storm.
episodes.183125: A broken line of strong to marginally severe thunderstorms moved into Northwest GA and continued southeast through the late afternoon and evening hours. Storms were strongest over parts of far northwest GA, and generally weakened as they moved to the southeast. Primary hazards included damaging winds with several reports of large hail as mid level lapse rates were rather steep.
episodes.183217: Surface high pressure was over the Lower Ohio Valley, but with an upper ridge centered over the CONUS, northwest flow moved several waves of convection through central Kentucky. This resulted in multiple wind damage and hail reports with limited flash flooding reports. A barn fire was also started by a lightning strike.
episodes.183232: An anomalously strong mid- and upper-level trough for early July was centered over the Plains and gradually moved eastward toward the Ohio Valley on July 1st and 2nd, 2023. A meandering surface frontal boundary gradually became more well defined throughout this period, with a warm front lifting through the Ohio Valley on July 1st before a series of remnant outflow boundaries and a convectively-enhanced cold frontal passage occurred July 2nd into the morning hours of July 3rd. Across central Kentucky and southern Indiana, there was ample fuel for convection, as temperatures in the mid-to-upper 80s and lower 90s and dewpoints in the low-to-mid 60s allowed for the development of over 2500 J/kg of mixed-layer CAPE. Since there was initially no predominant organizing feature for convection, multiple waves of showers and thunderstorms moved across the region on July 1st, producing intermittent instances of damaging straight-line winds and near-severe hail, primarily across southern Indiana. However, as the main trough and the surface cold front moved into the region on July 2nd, convection was better organized thanks to 40-45 knots of effective bulk shear in addition to moderate to high levels of instability. Convective development on July 2nd began during the early afternoon hours across southwestern Indiana and western Kentucky. Initially, convective mode was predominantly cellular, but cells gradually grew upscale through the afternoon into clusters and larger quasi-linear structures. Downdraft CAPE was over 1000 J/kg and significant hail parameter values exceeded 1 through most of the area; accordingly, strong to damaging winds and hail were the primary severe hazards observed during the afternoon and evening hours on July 2nd. However, there was just enough low-level helicity to facilitate the development of two weak tornadoes, one in Anderson County and the other in Casey County. Storms gradually subsided after sunset, with the severe threat ending across the region by midnight on July 3rd..
episodes.183265: The upper-level ridge over the Mid-South began to weaken and northwest flow aloft developed across the region. Outflow boundaries from earlier convection over Missouri helped trigger isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms over mainly the northern half of the Mid-South throughout the day into the evening. Adequate wind shear combined with strong instability helped some storms become severe with damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.183266: The upper-level ridge over the Mid-South began to weaken and northwest flow aloft developed across the region. Outflow boundaries from earlier convection over Missouri helped trigger isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms over mainly the northern half of the Mid-South throughout the day into the evening. Adequate wind shear combined with strong instability helped some storms become severe with damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.183281: A decaying complex of strong to severe thunderstorms pushed south-southwest through southern middle Tennessee during the mid evening hours. Gust front and outflow winds produced rather widespread damage in some areas of southern middle Tennessee.
episodes.183331: Widespread thunderstorms developed on the nose of a low-level jet. Much of the activity remained north of a stationary surface front. Some of the storms became severe with damaging winds. Also, isolated flash flooding was reported in Adams County.
episodes.183333: Even though an old outflow boundary was across southeast Missouri and the far southern portions of Illinois during the morning hours, the boundary dissipated, allowing 75+ dew points to surge north along the Mississippi River. As skies cleared the atmosphere was able to quickly destabilize. Surface based CAPEs were in excess of 3000 J/kg with 40kts of 0 to 6km bulk shear. This combined with a shortwave trough that moved eastward across the region, produced strong to severe storms. There were numerous reports of damaging winds and some reports of large hail. There were three fatalities due to fallen trees.
episodes.183334: Even though an old outflow boundary was across southeast Missouri and the far southern portions of Illinois during the morning hours, the boundary dissipated, allowing 75+ dew points to surge north along the Mississippi River. As skies cleared the atmosphere was able to quickly destabilize. Surface based CAPEs were in excess of 3000 J/kg with 40kts of 0 to 6km bulk shear. This combined with a shortwave trough that moved eastward across the region, produced strong to severe storms. There were numerous reports of damaging winds and some reports of large hail. episodes.183344: In early July there were significant reports of hail, damaging wind, and flash flooding. The month got off to a quick start with golf ball size hail just east of Omaha (Boone County) on the 1st. On the 5th, there was a 62 mph wind gust measured at Newport (Jackson County).
episodes.183348: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms, first from a decaying morning mesoscale convective system and later forming on outflow from earlier activity, produced heavy rainfall on July 1st. Instability was not high, but precipitable water values of 1.8 to 2.0 inches supported efficient rainfall. Localized totals of 1.5 to 2.5 inches, locally higher, produced flash flooding in several areas.
episodes.183349: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms, first from a decaying morning mesoscale convective system and later forming on outflow from earlier activity, produced heavy rainfall on July 1st. Instability was not high, but precipitable water values of 1.8 to 2.0 inches supported efficient rainfall. Localized totals of 1.5 to 2.5 inches, locally higher, produced flash flooding in several areas. Particularly hard hit was East Liverpool, with some home damage as a result of the flooding.
episodes.183368: An extremely moist and unstable summertime air mass was in place across Alabama on July 1st through July 2nd with excessive heat warnings and heat advisories in effect. PWAT's were also high with values near 2 inches, which produced high values for microburst potential. Several upper short wave troughs rotated around the north side of an upper ridge centered along the Gulf Coast, and triggered numerous strong to severe thunderstorms.
episodes.183369: The James River from the North Dakota and South Dakota border to near Ashton remained above flood stage through July. The river slowly decreased through the month due to below-average rainfall. Agricultural land and some county roadways continued to be impacted.
episodes.183444: Scattered severe thunderstorms associated with a weak surface trough produced damaging winds across portions of central and south central Virginia.
episodes.183552: A dying cluster of storms produced an isolated damaging wind gust on July 1st, 2023 in Saline county, Kansas.
episodes.183850: Two rounds of storms impacted eastern Kentucky on July 1st, 2023. The first was a MCS traveling from NW to SE across the state. This resulted in a couple rounds of storms and  wind damage in Powell and Montgomery Counties between 3:30 and 6:30am. The second set of storms developed along a warm front across the central and western portion of the state, and moved eastward throughout the afternoon, but did not result in any severe weather reports. However, the KY Mesonet station on Black Mountain did gust to 43 mph as one of the storms moved through.

episodes.183859: Slow moving thunderstorms produced flash flooding in the San Angelo area. Also, there was localized wind damage from an isolated severe thunderstorm in Junction.
episodes.183883: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of July 1st and produced one report of a severe wind gust.
episodes.183932: High based showers and thunderstorms associated with a shortwave passage brought strong wind gusts and some damage to portions of western and central Wyoming. Wind gusts to around 60 mph occurred in portions of Sublette, Teton and Big Horn Counties. Strong thunderstorm winds downed trees near the Grand Targhee Ski Resort in Teton County. Trees where reported down near Pinedale at the Boyd Skinner Park.
episodes.183947: Scattered thunderstorms developed over the North Carolina mountains and foothills during the afternoon. A few of the storms produced large hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.183948: Scattered thunderstorms developed near the Blue Ridge escarpment during the afternoon and moved southeast across the foothills and upper piedmont during the late afternoon and evening. A few of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts, including one significant downburst in the Pickens area.
episodes.183974: A Pacific system brought some severe weather mainly in the Upper Snake River Highlands region.
episodes.184179: Isolated thunderstorms formed across portions of eastern upper and northern lower Michigan during the afternoon as a seasonably strong shortwave progressed overhead. One of these thunderstorms produced wind gusts in excess of 34 kts over the St. Marys River.
episodes.184609: Developing showers and thunderstorms produced a brief landspout north of Sherwood, OH.

Thunderstorm winds caused significant tree and power line damage in St. Libory. One home sustained moderate roof damage due to a fallen tree. No deaths or injuries were reported.

Widespread wind damage occurred across most of Washington County. As the severe storm moved into the western portions of the county, several outbuildings and barns sustained major damage about 2 miles southwest of Johannisburg, along Illinois Route 15.  In Johannisburg, the steeple on St. Johns Evangelical Church was blown over onto the roof of the main church building causing catastrophic damage. In Venedy, widespread tree damage around town, a grain bin was damaged, as well as several power lines blown down. Three miles south southeast of Venedy, at the intersection of County Road 12 and Stone Church Road, a training center sustained major roof damage. About 3 miles south southwest of Okawville, a large barn was destroyed. Then just southwest of Okawville, multiple large treetops were snapped off and a barn and a machine shed were destroyed. Along County Highway 13, south of Okawville, two small barns were destroyed and two grain bins sustained minor damage. In Addieville, there was widespread tree and power line damage, as well as roof damage to a local business. As the storm moved into the Nashville area, numerous trees, tree limbs, power poles and power lines were blown down. One house sustained moderate roof damage due to a fallen tree. Also, a local business sustained roof damage with water causing interior damage as well. In Ashley, there was widespread tree, tree limbs and power lines blown down. One large tree fell onto a house causing moderate roof damage. Also, a number of trees were blown down onto Illinois Route 15. In Radom, a large tree was blown down onto a garage, destroying it.  No deaths or injuries were reported.

Widespread wind damage across the northern portions of St. Louis County as a line of storms moved through. Numerous large trees, tree limbs, power poles and power lines were blown down. In Jennings, a very large tree was snapped off (possibly due to a lightning strike) and landed on a home, crushing a 5 year old boy in his bedroom. He was rescued and taken to a nearby hospital, but was pronounced dead soon after. The house next door sustained major roof damage from this large tree as well.  A large tree branch, approximately two feet in diameter, was blown down onto an unoccupied car just east of Chesterfield. In Kirkwood, a large tree was uprooted and as it fell it damaged the corner of a home. Otherwise, widespread tree damage was reported in St. Ann, Clayton, University City, Creve Coeur, Overland, Florissant, Black Jack and Spanish Lake. Over 100,000 customers (St. Louis County/St. Louis City) were without power due to this storm. It took a little over 4 days to restore power to all of them.

A woman who was waiting for the storm to pass was killed when a large tree was blown over, crushing the car in the alley of the 4100 block of Chouteau Avenue. Two historical cemeteries, Calvary and Bellefontaine, sustained widespread damage. Around 100 trees at Calvary and nearly 40 significant trees and 100 smaller ones at Bellefontaine, were either uprooted or snapped off near the base, as well as numerous tree limbs. Several gravestones were either damaged or destroyed by fallen trees and/or tree limbs. A large tree was uprooted in the 3000 block of Longfellow Boulevard, landing on a house causing major roof damage. A couple of power poles were snapped off along Hall Street. The damage path began on the west side of U.S. Highway 45 near the community of Hickory. In this area, a pole was bent and there was major loss of roofing from a small barn. This is where the tornado was rated at its peak intensity of EF-1, with 90 mph winds. Along the rest of the path through Graves County, the only damage consisted of spotty broken branches and a few downed trees. The tornado exited into Marshall County northeast of the community of Clear Springs.
A severe thunderstorm producing winds estimated near 60 mph blew off a section of metal roof and knocked down power lines. Debris was blown across Route 281 near Friedens.

The weak tornado crossed into Marshall County from Graves County near the small community of Oak Level. There were numerous trees and power lines down east of Highway 641 to the Kentucky Lake shore. Damage in western Marshall County consisted of spotty broken tree branches and a few downed trees. Peak winds were estimated near 80 mph in Marshall County. The tornado exited into Lyon County after it moved over Kentucky Lake east of the Moors Camp area.
Idaho Highway 33 was blocked in both directions at milepost 141 due to multiple power lines downed.

The weak tornado crossed Kentucky Lake from Marshall County and entered Lyon County in the Land-Between-The-Lakes National Recreation Area. The apparent damage path ended at the Twin Lakes campground, which is along the Kentucky Lake shore about two miles south of the canal between Lake Barkley and Kentucky Lake. Numerous campers were destroyed, and trees were downed. Peak winds in Lyon County were estimated near 80 mph. Witnesses in the area reported seeing funnel clouds.
